canada.title: Police identify suspect vehicle tied to midtown shooting, home invasion that killed Toronto musician
canada.summary: Toronto police have identified a suspect vehicle tied to a fatal shooting and attempted home invasion that took place early Wednesday in midtown Toronto.

canada.title: Eastern Shore residents fight to protect Lawrencetown Beach Hill after property goes up for sale
canada.summary: Amy DeBaie started a petition to save "one of the most beautiful places on the Eastern Shore."

canada.title: Opposition accuses PC of ‘skirting the rules’ to pay political staffer, PCs says they’re ‘chasing unicorns’
canada.summary: The Liberals are accusing the PCs of misusing government funds to pay consultant Steve Outhouse as Government House leader Lloyd Parrott fired back that the opposition is ‘grasping at straws.’

canada.title: How do firearms seized over mental health concerns get returned, like in the Tumbler Ridge case?
canada.summary: There’s been a lot of debate surrounding the return of seized firearms taken from the home of the Tumbler Ridge shooter, especially after a recent U.S. court filing suggested Jesse Van Rootselaar used those guns in the mass shooting.

canada.title: Driving instructor arrested for alleged sexual assault in Longueuil, Que.
canada.summary: The alleged assault occurred on Nov. 13 in the Saint-Hubert borough of Longueuil, where Dagenais was working as a driving instructor, according to police.

canada.title: Edmonton city council to receive report on options for adhering to provincial direction on infill
canada.summary: Edmonton city council is set to hammer out new rules around infill that could include tighter restrictions on where row housing and multiplexes can be built, and also lay out requirements for parking minimums.

canada.title: NDP caucus to take oath in Victoria while Eby to be sworn in separately
canada.summary: New Democrats will be sworn into office in the British Columbia legislature Thursday but former premier David Eby won't be among them.

canada.title: Mayor’s Kraft Dinner comments prompt second protest at City Hall
canada.summary: After starting a swirl of memes, mockery and malcontent over Kraft Dinner comments, Montreal Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada will witness protesters on Thursday afternoon in front of City Hall.

canada.title: Alberta health officials to give update on soldiers injured in CFB Wainwright fire
canada.summary: The military has said a windstorm on Oct. 17 pushed flames from a grass fire onto troops in a training exercise at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, southeast of Edmonton.

canada.title: Easier access to psilocybin therapy needed, patients and health experts say
canada.summary: Advocates in Saskatchewan spoke about their experiences with psychedelic therapy on Wednesday's Blue Sky.

canada.title: Sask. government introduces bill to 'protect infrastructure' against occupations, blockades
canada.summary: Saskatchewan introduced a bill Wednesday intended to protect economic infrastructure against "illegal occupations, disruptions and blockades."

canada.title: Students welcome plan to revive Aurora College social work program — but say it should be in Fort Smith
canada.summary: Haidyn Allingham and Austin Blanchard are both currently enrolled in a prerequisite diploma program in Fort Smith and now may have to move to Yellowknife next year if they want to continue pursuing social work degrees.

canada.title: Winnipeg neighbourhood group wants stronger enforcement of city's infill housing rules
canada.summary: A group of Winnipeg residents is calling for better infill design and more enforcement of the city's regulations. The Glenwood Neighbourhood Association says it's not opposed to infill, but wants it done properly.

canada.title: Court documents reveal details of Winnipeg man's alleged Bishnoi gang extortion
canada.summary: A man accused of extorting someone on behalf of an Indian organized crime group allegedly used a payphone in Winnipeg's south St. Vital area to demand money from his victim, before mailing a letter to the man's home threatening his family.

canada.title: A look inside N.B. Power’s nerve centre
canada.summary: The system operators of the energy control centre have to balance outages, both planned and unplanned, with the available power from generating assets and neighbouring electrical grids to provide homes and businesses with the power they need.

canada.title: Governor General to make first official visit to N.B. this week
canada.summary: During her first official visit to the province, Gov. Gen. Louise Arbour has plans to meet provincial officials and members of the Canadian Armed Forces in Fredericton and Base Gagetown.

canada.title: Why the large majority of new housing construction in Halifax is for the rental market
canada.summary: As of October, the large majority of housing starts in Halifax have been for units destined for the rental market. Experts say government incentives, planning policies and affordability are some reasons for this trend.

canada.title: Group so far unable to get green light for final section of Bonavista Peninsula ATV trail
canada.summary: An ATV trails group has the support of communities on the Bonavista Peninsula to develop the old railbed. However, the province has not granted them a four-to five kilometre section in an unincorporated community that would connect north and south sections of the network.

lines: Good morning. I’m Hannah Thibedeau, and this is your Palindrome News brief.
Prime Minister Mark Carney says the Pentagon’s recent complaints about Canada’s defence spending have not come up in his conversations with U.S, The Canadian Press reports.
The Big Story speaks with Diana Swain, contributing correspondent for Dateline Canada, about the state of the Elizabeth Bain case, CityNews Winnipeg reports.
Zelenskyy warns of imminent major Russian attack on Ukraine’s power grid, The Canadian Press reports.
Macy’s 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade will also be a first: Organizers made an unprecedented decision to postpone the event to Saturday because of bad weather, The Associated Press reports.

China, Japan and other U.S. trading partners protested planned tariff hikes by the Trump administration and hit back Thursday at allegations they have excess manufacturing capacity, The Canadian Press reports.
That’s your brief. We’ll keep watching, so you don’t have to.
